lots.what_it_is: Two groups of Victorian tea ware, about 25 pieces: (1) Wedgwood blue transfer printed fluted bone china tea and dessert ware with gilt rims and a neoclassical swag border, base printed with the blue Portland vase over WEDGWOOD mark (1880s type, no date code or pattern name seen), about 15 pieces; (2) an unmarked Imari palette 'gaudy willow' group, one plate and about three trios of coffee cans, saucers and plates, about 10 pieces.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2: printed blue Portland vase over WEDGWOOD on a fluted cup base, no ENGLAND, no date letters legible, ring of brown spotting/staining round the foot rim of that cup. Photo 1: blue and white group is one large moulded plate, a stack of side plates, saucers and about five cups; Imari group is one plate plus three coffee cans on saucers and plates. Photo 3: Imari cans in orange red, cobalt and gilt willow scene, gilt rubbed on rims. No maker mark shown on the Imari group.
lots.condition: Brown spotting round the base of at least one fluted cup, gilt wear on rims of both groups; chips or hairlines cannot be ruled out from the photos.
lots.question_for_armitage: Please confirm the piece count for each group, whether any cups or plates are chipped, cracked or stained (the fluted cup in photo 2 has brown spotting round the foot), and whether the Imari pieces carry any backstamp.
